tools.name: configure_python_environment
tools.description: This tool configures a Python environment in the given workspace. ALWAYS Use this tool to set up the user's chosen environment and ALWAYS call this tool before using any other Python related tools or running any Python command in the terminal. IMPORTANT: This tool is only for Python environments (venv, virtualenv, conda, pipenv, poetry, pyenv, pixi, or any other Python environment manager). Do not use this tool for npm packages, system packages, Ruby gems, or any other non-Python dependencies.

resourcePath.description: The path to the Python file or workspace for which a Python Environment needs to be configured.

tools.name: get_python_environment_details
tools.description: This tool will retrieve the details of the Python Environment for the specified file or workspace. The details returned include the 1. Type of Python Environment (conda, venv, etc), 2. Version of Python, 3. List of all installed Python packages with their versions. ALWAYS call configure_python_environment before using this tool. IMPORTANT: This tool is only for Python environments (venv, virtualenv, conda, pipenv, poetry, pyenv, pixi, or any other Python environment manager). Do not use this tool for npm packages, system packages, Ruby gems, or any other non-Python dependencies.

resourcePath.description: The path to the Python file or workspace to get the environment information for.

tools.name: get_python_executable_details
tools.description: This tool will retrieve the details of the Python Environment for the specified file or workspace. ALWAYS use this tool before executing any Python command in the terminal. This tool returns the details of how to construct the fully qualified path and or command including details such as arguments required to run Python in a terminal. Note: Instead of executing `python --version` or `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'`, use this tool to get the Python executable path to replace the `python` command. E.g. instead of using `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'`, use this tool to build the command `conda run -n <env_name> -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'`. ALWAYS call configure_python_environment before using this tool. IMPORTANT: This tool is only for Python environments (venv, virtualenv, conda, pipenv, poetry, pyenv, pixi, or any other Python environment manager). Do not use this tool for npm packages, system packages, Ruby gems, or any other non-Python dependencies.

resourcePath.description: The path to the Python file or workspace to get the executable information for. If not provided, the current workspace will be used. Where possible pass the path to the file or workspace.

tools.name: install_python_packages
tools.description: Installs Python packages in the given workspace. Use this tool to install Python packages in the user's chosen Python environment. ALWAYS call configure_python_environment before using this tool. IMPORTANT: This tool should only be used to install Python packages using package managers like pip or conda (works with any Python environment: venv, virtualenv, pipenv, poetry, pyenv, pixi, conda, etc.). Do not use this tool to install npm packages, system packages (apt/brew/yum), Ruby gems, or any other non-Python dependencies.

packageList.description: The list of Python packages to install.

resourcePath.description: The path to the Python file or workspace into which the packages are installed. If not provided, the current workspace will be used. Where possible pass the path to the file or workspace.

tools.name: container-tools_get-config
tools.description: Gets the configuration the user has set for the container and container orchestrator (compose) CLIs, including the correct base commands to use and any environment variables that will be set. This tool **MUST** be called before generating or running any container or container orchestrator CLI commands, to ensure the correct base command is used.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceAnalyze
tools.description: Pylance code-flow analysis for Python. One tool that dispatches between commands for tracing, typing, and visualizing program state. Commands: "traceValue" — walk the program flow graph backwards from a position to explain how a variable got its value (assignments, narrowing, try/except). Use when the user asks "where does this value come from?" or "what does this depend on?". "typeAt" — get the inferred/narrowed Python type at a position (lighter than `pylanceLSP textDocument/hover`, returns only the type). "flowGraph" — return an ASCII visualization of the code-flow graph at a position; useful for debugging unexpected narrowing or branch behavior. "traceFailure" — trace value provenance across multiple stack frames (caller-supplied, innermost-first); bridges through function-parameter boundaries by resolving the matching argument at each call site. "tracePytestFailure" — paste raw pytest failure output and the tool extracts frames, assertions, and variables automatically and runs traceFailure for each failure. "help" — full per-command parameter reference. Prefer `pylanceLSP textDocument/definition` for "where is this defined?"; use this tool for value provenance across reassignments and conditions, not symbol resolution. Positions are LSP 0-based `{ line, character }`; URIs must be `file://` and inside the workspace.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

command.description: Analysis command to run. Use "help" for full per-command documentation, parameters, and examples.

fileUri.description: LSP file URI (e.g. "file:///workspace/foo.py") or absolute path. Required for traceValue, typeAt, flowGraph.

position.description: LSP-style 0-based position. Required for traceValue, typeAt, flowGraph.

symbol.description: Variable/symbol name to trace. Required for traceValue.

transitive.description: For traceValue/traceFailure/tracePytestFailure: if true, recursively trace RHS dependencies (slower, deeper). Default: false for traceValue, true for traceFailure/tracePytestFailure.

transitiveDepth.description: For traceValue: max recursion depth when transitive=true. Default: 3.

frames.description: Stack frames innermost-first. Required for traceFailure.

variables.description: Variable names to trace at the innermost frame. Required for traceFailure.

assertion.description: Optional for traceFailure: assertion text used to enrich variable extraction.

pytestOutput.description: Raw pytest failure output (full or just FAILURES section). Max 1 MB. Required for tracePytestFailure.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceCheckSignatureCompatibility
tools.description: Check whether existing call sites are compatible with a function or method's current signature and return type. Prefer this over text search or manual sampling because Pylance combines semantic references, import-alias following, and per-call-site type checking. Use before or after signature changes; wrappers and other indirect call surfaces may need separate checks with this tool or pylanceLSP references.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

fileUri.description: The uri of the file containing the modified function.

line.description: The 0-based line number of the function.

character.description: The 0-based character offset within the line.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceDocuments
tools.description: Retrieve Pylance documentation for troubleshooting, configuration, and diagnostic rules. Two actions: "search" — finds relevant documentation for a natural language query. Returns a list of document paths with metadata. "fetch" — retrieves a specific document by its doc-root-relative path. Returns local file path, size, and cross-references. For doc-grounded answers, search first, then fetch relevant paths. Fetch returns a localPath you can read; set includeContent=true when inline content is cheaper than a separate file read. Returned references are doc-root-relative paths; fetch them through this tool when you need their localPath, size, or content. Prefer this over web search or raw file guessing because it resolves curated Pylance doc paths and cross-references directly.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

action.description: Action to perform. "search" finds relevant docs for a query. "fetch" retrieves a specific document by path.

query.description: Required for "search". A natural language question about Pylance.

includeContent.description: Optional for "fetch". If true, includes the document content in the response. Default: false.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceFileSyntaxErrors
tools.description: Check a Python file for syntax errors. Returns detailed error list with line numbers, messages, and error types. Use when: users report Python syntax problems, validating Python files before processing, debugging parse errors.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

fileUri.description: The uri of the Python file to check for syntax errors. Must be a user file in the workspace.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceImports
tools.description: Analyze imports across all Pylance user files in a workspace, returning top-level modules that are found and not found. Prefer this over grep/source walks for project import audits because it uses the editor workspace, Pylance import resolution, and a single deduplicated scan. Use with pylanceInstalledTopLevelModules for requirements/dependency audits: compare all imported modules (found and not found) with installed modules and declared dependencies. Installed/importable can still be undeclared, and unresolved can still be declared but missing from the selected interpreter. Use LSP diagnostics only when locations, severities, or report codes are needed.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceInvokeRefactoring
tools.description:
Apply named Pylance refactorings to a Python file, including unused-import cleanup, import-format/star/module conversion, inferred type annotations, shadowed-stdlib import renames, and fix-all. Prefer this over hand edits for these operations because Pylance uses symbol and import resolution that text rewrites cannot safely reconstruct. Modes: "update" applies edits, "edits" previews a WorkspaceEdit, and "string" returns updated content; default is "update". Available refactorings: source.unusedImports: - Removes all unused import statements from a Python file. Use when imports are imported but never referenced in the code. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with unused imports.
source.optionalMemberAccessAssert: - Inserts assert statements like `assert x is not None` before statements that access members on optional receivers. Use when optional member access diagnostics should be narrowed automatically across a file. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with optional member access diagnostics.
source.convertImportFormat: - Converts import statements between absolute and relative formats according to python.analysis.importFormat setting. Use when import format consistency is needed. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with imports to convert.
source.convertImportStar: - Converts all wildcard imports (from module import *) to explicit imports listing all imported symbols. Use when explicit imports are preferred for better code clarity and IDE support. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with wildcard imports.
source.convertImportToModule: - Converts `from module import name1, name2` (including wildcard imports) into `import module` and rewrites references to `module.name1`, `module.name2`. Use when you want module-qualified references. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with `from ... import ...` statements.
source.renameShadowedStdlibImports: - Renames imported user modules that shadow standard library module names (e.g. a local calendar.py). Use to avoid import shadowing bugs. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to the importing Python file.
source.addTypeAnnotation: - Adds type annotations to all variables and functions in a Python file that can be inferred from their usage. Use when type hints are needed for better type checking and code clarity. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with unannotated variables or functions.
source.fixAll.pylance: - Applies all available automatic code fixes from python.analysis.fixAll setting. Use when multiple code issues need to be addressed simultaneously. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to a Python file with fixable issues.
workspace.generateDependencies: - Analyzes Python imports in the workspace and generates or updates a dependency file (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, requirements.in, environment.yml). Use when you need to create or update dependency files based on actual code imports. Requires fileUri parameter pointing to the workspace root. Optional parameters: format ("requirements.txt" | "pyproject.toml" | "pyproject.toml-poetry" | "requirements.in" | "environment.yml" | "auto"), versionPin ("exact" | "compatible" | "none"), syncMode (boolean to remove stale deps).

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

fileUri.description: The uri of the Python file to invoke the refactoring. For workspace.generateDependencies, this should be the workspace root uri.

name.description: The name of the refactoring to invoke. This must be one of these [source.unusedImports, source.optionalMemberAccessAssert, source.convertImportFormat, source.convertImportStar, source.convertImportToModule, source.renameShadowedStdlibImports, source.addTypeAnnotation, source.fixAll.pylance, workspace.generateDependencies]

mode.description: Determines the output mode: "update" updates the file directly, "edits" returns a WorkspaceEdit, "string" returns the updated content as a string. If omitted, "update" will be used as the default. The "edits" mode is especially useful for checking if any changes are needed (such as unused imports or import formatting issues) without modifying the file, as it will return a WorkspaceEdit only if edits are required.

format.description: Only for workspace.generateDependencies: dependency file format. "auto" detects from existing files. Defaults to "auto".

versionPin.description: Only for workspace.generateDependencies: version pinning strategy. "exact" pins to ==X.Y.Z, "compatible" uses >=X.Y or ^X.Y.Z, "none" omits versions. Defaults to format-specific default.

syncMode.description: Only for workspace.generateDependencies: when true, removes packages from the dependency file that are not found in code. Defaults to false (merge-only).

enablePypiLookup.description: Only for workspace.generateDependencies: when true, queries PyPI as a last resort for unknown import→package mappings. Defaults to true.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylanceLSP
tools.description: Read-only Pylance/Pyright LSP access for Python using the workspace editor state and selected interpreter. Use for cross-file Python code intelligence: find all references to a function/class, rename-impact analysis, every caller/call site, call hierarchy, definitions, document/workspace symbols, hover/type/signature info, and Pylance diagnostics. Parameters follow LSP: file paths are `file:///...` URIs; positions and ranges are 0-based `{ line, character }`; most textDocument methods need `{ textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }`. Diagnostics: use `textDocument/diagnostic` for one file and read each `Diagnostic.code` for the exact `reportXxx` Pylance rule, such as `reportArgumentType` or `reportOptionalMemberAccess`, before explaining or fixing any reported error. It takes `{ textDocument: { uri } }` and returns `{ kind: "full", items: Diagnostic[] }`. Use `workspace/diagnostic` with `{}` to enumerate diagnostics across the whole workspace in one call when the user wants project-wide errors instead of walking files; its response is `{ items: [{ uri, kind: "full", items: Diagnostic[] }, ...] }`, so inspect every returned file entry. Include diagnostic messages, severities, codes, and ranges when the user asks about Pylance problems. Relationships: use `textDocument/references` for rename impact analysis and all usages, including aliased/re-exported call sites. Use `callHierarchy/prepare` then `callHierarchy/incomingCalls` or `callHierarchy/outgoingCalls` to trace callers, callees, or bug propagation across functions. Use type hierarchy for class ancestry. Navigation and facts: use `textDocument/definition`, `declaration`, `typeDefinition`, or `implementation` for targets; use `textDocument/hover` and `textDocument/signatureHelp` for inferred types and call parameters; use `textDocument/documentSymbol` or `workspace/symbol` to enumerate symbols; use highlights, inlay hints, semantic tokens, code lens, folding, colors, and selections when those exact editor facts are requested. For requirements.txt or dependency audits, prefer `pylanceImports` plus `pylanceInstalledTopLevelModules`; use diagnostics only when locations, severities, exact rule codes, or workspace problem lists matter. Use method `help` for the full 31-method reference with exact parameters, response shapes, and less-common methods.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

method.description: The LSP method to invoke. Use "help" for full documentation of all methods, parameters, and responses.

params.description: LSP parameters object for the method. Shape follows the LSP specification. Most textDocument/* methods require { textDocument: { uri }, position: { line, character } }.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylancePythonDebug

Prefer this over terminal `python -m debugpy`, pdb, or raw DAP setup because it uses the workspace/editor interpreter and manages debug session plumbing. Use for runtime bugs that need frame inspection; use pylanceRunCodeSnippet for one-shot expression or value checks. Set useUv for uv/PEP 723 projects. Actions: start, command, stop, list, help.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

action.description: Action to perform. start: begin a debug session; command: send debug command; stop: end session; list: show active sessions; help: show usage.

args.description: Arguments to pass to the script/module.

cwd.description: Working directory for the debug session.

pythonPath.description: Path to Python interpreter. Auto-detected if omitted.

justMyCode.description: Only debug user code, skip library code. Default: true.

exceptionFilters.description: Exception breakpoint filters. raised: break on all exceptions; uncaught: break on unhandled; userUnhandled: break on user-unhandled.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in ms for run command. Default: 600000 (10 min).

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylancePythonProfileExplorer
tools.description: Explore Python-native profiling artifacts captured by pylancePythonProfiling. Supports loader/query/release/reset actions with paged text-based exploration for Tachyon CPU captures, sys.monitoring traces, and Memray-derived memory summaries. Views intentionally follow a familiar profiling-explorer pattern while remaining honest about Python-specific artifact semantics.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

filePath.description: Path to a profiling artifact or sidecar metadata file. Absolute or workspace-relative.

profileId.description: Profile handle returned from load* actions.

view.description: Query view name. CPU: summary|callTree|bottomUp|eventLog|search|nodeContext. Trace: summary|events|byCategory|byProcessThread|timelineSlices|search. Heap: summary|allocations|search.

queryText.description: Search text for search views. Syntax: space-separated terms use OR; +term requires AND; /regex/ for regex; "phrase" for exact match. Example: "foo +bar /^init/". `/regex/` is a safe, case-insensitive subset (no back-references, look-around, `\b`, `\xHH`/`\uHHHH`, `\p{...}`, or flags); unsupported or malformed patterns fall back to a literal substring match.

tools.name: mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylancePythonProfiling
tools.description: Capture Python-native profiling artifacts. Provides CPU profiling via Python 3.15 Tachyon/profiling.sampling, event tracing via sys.monitoring, and memory captures via Memray when installed in the selected interpreter. Keeps an action-based MCP surface similar to the TypeScript profiling tools while using Python-specific backends and artifact semantics. Python-specific tweaks include profilingSessionId-based lifecycle management, explicit launch/attach target parameters, and actionable prerequisite failures.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional workspace root for this tool call. Standalone MCP uses this before the server --workspace argument.

mode.description: Profiling mode. launch: start a target process. attach: attach to an existing Python process (currently CPU profiling only).

module.description: Python module to profile with -m (launch mode).

args.description: Arguments to pass to the target script/module.

cwd.description: Working directory for the profiled target.

pythonPath.description: Path to the Python interpreter. Relative paths resolve against the selected target/workspace when possible; auto-detected if omitted.

pid.description: Target process ID for attach mode.

label.description: Human-readable label for the profiling session.

regionStartLocation.description: startCpuRegion only: region start as "file:line". When execution first reaches this line the target parks, Tachyon attaches, then the region runs sampled from its first instruction.

regionStopLocation.description: startCpuRegion only: region stop as "file:line". When execution reaches this line the sampler is detached/flushed before the target resumes, so only the region is captured.

regionMarkers.description: startCpuRegion only: optional sub-region markers as "label@file:line" (or "file:line"). Each time execution reaches a marker line inside the region, a labeled timestamp (ms from region start) is recorded into metadata so the profile explorer can slice to sub-regions without re-attaching.

profilingSessionId.description: Profiling session ID (required for status/stopCpu/stopTracing/stop when targeting an existing session).

samplingRate.description: Sampling rate for Tachyon CPU profiling, such as "1khz" or "500hz". Default: 1khz.

duration.description: Tachyon CPU sampling duration in seconds. Useful for bounding attach-mode captures. Default: run to completion.

samplingMode.description: Tachyon sampling mode: wall (all samples), cpu (on-CPU only), gil (holds GIL), exception (active exception). Default: cpu.

allThreads.description: Capture all threads for supported backends.

native.description: Include native frames where supported by the backend.

blocking.description: Use Tachyon blocking sampling mode for more consistent stacks at higher target overhead. Not supported on Windows (the CPython blocking path hangs); rejected with an error there.

noGc.description: Omit artificial <GC> frames from Tachyon CPU samples (maps to --no-gc).

opcodes.description: Gather bytecode opcode information for instruction-level Tachyon CPU profiling.

traceCalls.description: Include Python call events in sys.monitoring traces. Default: true.

traceReturns.description: Include Python return/resume/yield events in sys.monitoring traces. Default: true.

traceExceptions.description: Include exception events in sys.monitoring traces. Default: true.

traceLines.description: Include line events in sys.monitoring traces. Disabled by default because event volume can be very high.

traceInstructions.description: Include instruction-level events in sys.monitoring traces. Disabled by default.

traceBranches.description: Include branch and jump events in sys.monitoring traces. Disabled by default.

verboseLogging.description: Enable verbose logging for profiler orchestration.

tools.name: activate_prisma_migrate_development
tools.description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group consists of two Prisma Migrate tools designed for managing database schema migrations during development. The `prisma-migrate-dev` tool is used to synchronize the database schema with the Prisma schema file (`schema.prisma`). It performs a multi-step process: first, it re-runs existing migrations in a shadow database to detect any drift caused by manual edits or deleted migration files; second, it applies any pending migrations from colleagues; third, it generates a new migration from recent schema changes; fourth, it applies all unapplied migrations to the development database; and finally, it triggers artifact generation (e.g., Prisma Client). The complementary tool, `prisma-migrate-reset`, is used to forcefully reset the database and migration history when drift is detected or a clean slate is needed. It drops the database (or performs a soft reset if dropping is not possible), creates a new schema, applies all migrations, and runs seed scripts. This reset tool should only be used on development databases and never on production. Together, these tools enable a smooth development workflow where schema changes can be iterated and validated quickly, with the ability to start fresh when migration history becomes inconsistent.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

tools.name: activate_prisma_platform_setup
tools.description:
Call this tool when you need access to a new category of tools. The category of tools is described as follows:

This group contains tools for setting up and managing online Prisma Postgres databases via the Prisma Platform. The `prisma-platform-login` tool handles authentication by logging in an existing user or creating a new account, which is a prerequisite for using Prisma Postgres services. The `prisma-postgres-create-database` tool allows the creation of a new online Postgres database, requiring a user-specified name and a region selection from a list that includes us-east-1, eu-west-3, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1, or by calling without a region to get updated options. If the workspace plan limit is reached, the tool returns guidance: the user can either connect to an existing database via the Prisma Console (console.prisma.io) to obtain a connection string, upgrade their plan, or delete unused databases. These tools work sequentially: first ensure the user is logged in, then create the database in an appropriate region. They are essential for initializing a Prisma Postgres environment for development or production use.

Be sure to call this tool if you need a capability related to the above.

tools.name: prisma-migrate-status

The prisma migrate status command looks up the migrations in ./prisma/migrations/* folder and the entries in the _prisma_migrations table and compiles information about the state of the migrations in your database.
Use this tool instead of running `prisma migrate status` on the CLI.
Example output:

Status
3 migrations found in prisma/migrations

Your local migration history and the migrations table from your database are different:

The last common migration is: 20201127134938_new_migration

The migration have not yet been applied:
20201208100950_test_migration

The migrations from the database are not found locally in prisma/migrations:
20201208100950_new_migration

tools.name: prisma-migrate-dev
tools.description:
Prisma Migrate Dev is used to update Prisma whenever the schema.prisma file has been modified.
Use this tool instead of running `prisma migrate dev` on the CLI.
Always provide a descriptive name argument describing the change that was made to the Prisma Schema.
The migrate dev command performs these steps:
1. Reruns the existing migration history in the shadow database in order to detect schema drift (edited or deleted migration file, or a manual changes to the database schema)
2. Applies pending migrations to the shadow database (for example, new migrations created by colleagues)
3. Generates a new migration from any changes you made to the Prisma schema before running migrate dev
4. Applies all unapplied migrations to the development database and updates the _prisma_migrations table
5. Triggers the generation of artifacts (for example, Prisma Client)
